messages:
nina: quick sync — noticed a regression in prefix/prompt cache hit-rate after the recent kernel-selector change. sending profiling summary below, want thoughts on slab affinity + prefetcher interplay

sam: regression how big? did selector change alter kv key layout or kernel memory allocation pattern?

nina: p95 latency ~+18% on inference paths that rely on prefix cache. overall prefix cache hit_rate dropped from ~58% -> ~42% on sampled prod traces. evictions and fragmentation both up. suspect slab affinity + different allocation batch sizes causing key shadowing.

kevin: can you paste the profiler dump / numbers?

nina: sure — pasted from perf-bot run (trimmed)

```
-- KV Cache Profiler --
trace: prod/infra/2026-11-03/09:12
total_requests: 624000
prefix_hits: 266000
prefix_misses: 358000
hit_rate: 42.6%
evictions/sec: 85
avg_slab_util: 72%
fragmentation: 14.2%
gpu_mem_pressure: 78%
cpu_mem_pressure: 21%
median_key_size: 512B
hot_cohort_10pct_hitrate: 55%
```

kevin: ugh. fragmentation 14% + avg_slab_util 72% is suspicious. sounds like we pinned some prefixes to narrow slabs and new allocation pattern left holes. kernel selector change bumped continuous-batch window -> different sequence lengths which shift key sizes. slab affinity can make that worse if hot_prefixes map to small slabs and then evict other items.

anya: what about the prefetcher? is it disabled? we rely on prefetch warmup in low throughput regions.

nina: prefetcher was enabled, but its window_ms was tuned down in the same deploy (120 -> 40ms) to reduce burstiness. short window + slab affinity seemed to reduce opportunity for migration/warmup. we ran a quick local canary adjusting those two knobs.

kevin: experiment results (canary id: canary-3) — changed slab_affinity=balanced (instead of strict), prefetcher.window_ms=200ms, enabled keystate_shadow=true (keeps small cpu-side shadow copy for hot keys and async migrate to GPU). results:

```
canary-3: 6h run on prod-sampled traffic
total_requests: 48k
prefix_hits: 34.2k
prefix_misses: 13.8k
hit_rate: 71.3% (+28.7pp)
evictions/sec: 48 (-43%)
fragmentation: 6.1% (-8.1pp)
gpu_mem_pressure: 63% (-15pp)
p95_latency: -22% (relative improvement)
oom_events: 0
```

sam: that's a massive improvement. what's the memory overhead for keystate_shadow? doubling some metadata?

kevin: measured ~+7% CPU mem overhead for the shadow index and async migration buffer. we cap shadow size by cohort (hot top-3% prefixes). implementation keeps only key metadata + small prefetch payload until migrated.

nina: important tradeoff note: shadowing reduces fragmentation by keeping hot keys continuous in the GPU slab during migration windows and lets compaction run during low-load periods. we saw compaction throughput spike ~10% but within acceptable limits.

anya: can we break down the hit-rate delta by prefix-length cohort? are short prefixes benefitting more?

kevin: yes — short prefixes (<128 tokens) benefited most. hit-rate by cohort: short 82% -> 90% on canary, mid 54% -> 70%, long 28% -> 45%. overall skewed toward short/mid since they're ~78% of requests.

nina: commands/config we used to run the canary (for reproducibility):

```yaml
cache:
  slab_affinity: balanced
  compaction:
    enabled: true
    throttle_pct: 0.1
  prefetcher:
    enabled: true
    window_ms: 200
    min_suffix_count: 2
  keystate_shadow:
    enabled: true
    max_shadow_pct: 3
    migrate_batch: 64
```

# rollout snippet
redwoodctl rollout start --service=runtime --canary=canary-3 --config=eng-runtime/keystate-shadow-200ms.yaml
```

sam: any regressions observed? wrong corner cases?

kevin: a couple: 1) under very low throughput the shadowing didn't migrate fast enough and we saw slightly higher CPU usage; mitigated by lowering migrate_batch and reducing max_shadow_pct. 2) a rare race when compaction and async migrate hit same slab, we added a lightweight slab lock to serialize compaction vs migrate. both fixes are in the canary branch.

nina: risk matrix:
- data correctness: none (purely caching/warmup)
- cost: +7% CPU mem on average; small extra compaction cycles
- latency: improved for p95 but tail can regress if migrate backlog forms -> need backpressure

anya: sounds reasonable. what's next for rollout plan?

nina: proposal:
1) run canary-3 for 48h across two regions (us-west, eu-central)
2) add synthetic stress test to exercise low-throughput+high-sparsity patterns
3) add metric alert if migrate_backlog > 5000 keys or slab_lock contention > 1%
4) if green, ramp to 20% traffic -> monitor evictions and fragmentation for 24h -> full rollout

kevin: I've opened the PR with tests and e2e script. perf-bot posted the last automated run: \"perf-bot: canary-3 run complete, improvement validated vs baseline (p<0.01)\" :tada:

nina: cool. can someone pick up the alert and dashboard work? we need: migrate_backlog, slab_lock_contention, per-cohort hitrate, avg_slab_util, fragmentation, evictions/sec.

sam: I'll take dashboard. will add alert thresholds and link to runbook.

anya: I'll validate cost model with finance for +7% CPU delta and ensure dedicated customers are informed (opt-in for private)

kevin: one more thought — we should capture a fallback flag to disable keystate_shadow per-tenant if they hit memory constraints. easy config toggle.

nina: agreed. assigning follow-ups in the thread: @sam dashboard + alerts, @anya cost/comms, @kevin follow-up PR for slab_lock metrics + fallback toggle. thanks everyone, let's sync in 24h on canary health. :white_check_mark:
